cards.text: Paul, the apostle (1 Corinthians 1:1), is still writing to the church in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:2) about tongues and prophecy. Now he asks, "What then shall we say, brothers?" When they come together, everyone brings something: a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue or an interpretation.

cards.question: When the Corinthian church comes together, everybody brings a psalm, a teaching, a tongue or something else. What does Paul say all of it must do?

cards.text: First up is speaking in tongues, and Paul puts a NUMBER on it: two, or at most three, taking turns. Good, because the whole room going at once isn't a meeting, friend, it's a group chat with ninety-nine unread messages.

cards.question: The people speaking in a tongue in Corinth take turns. What else does Paul say must happen?

cards.text: But what if nobody in the room can interpret? Paul's got a plan for that too.

cards.question: True or false: in Corinth, when there's no interpreter, Paul says the one with a tongue should stay silent in the church.

cards.text: He should speak only to himself and God. Next come the prophets, and two or three of them should speak.

cards.question: True or false: while two or three prophets speak in the Corinthian meeting, Paul says the others should weigh carefully what is said.

cards.text: Now picture a prophet mid-message, and suddenly someone sitting down gets a revelation. This is the work meeting where two people start talking at once and then do the "no, YOU go" dance for ten straight minutes.

cards.question: A prophet in Corinth is speaking, and a revelation comes to someone seated. What does Paul say should happen?

cards.text: Then Paul says they can ALL prophesy, one at a time. Same as my oven, friend: every batch gets in, just not all at once.

cards.question: Paul says the prophets in Corinth can all prophesy in turn. Why?

answers.text: So the leaders stay in charge
So the meeting ends on time

cards.text: Then Paul adds one short line: "The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets." Short line, friend, but chew on it slow, like the last cookie in the box.

cards.question: Paul gives the reason behind all this taking turns: God is not a God of disorder, but of ___.
True or false: right after calling God a God of peace, Paul mentions only the church in Corinth.

cards.text: Next, Paul writes, "Women are to be silent in the churches." He says they are not permitted to speak but must be in submission.

cards.question: Paul writes that women must be in submission in the churches, and he points to something that says so. What is it?

cards.text: If women wish to inquire about something, Paul says they are to ask their own husbands at home. He says it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
Then Paul asks two questions: "Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?"

cards.question: True or false: Paul says anyone in Corinth who thinks he's a prophet or spiritual should acknowledge that what Paul is writing is the Lord's command.
Paul then warns about anyone in Corinth who ignores what he's writing. What does he say happens to that person?

cards.text: Now Paul starts to wrap it all up, and he calls them his brothers. That's the oven timer going DING, friend, and it's time to pull the batch out.

cards.question: In his wrap-up, Paul tells his brothers in Corinth to be eager to ___.
True or false: in his wrap-up, Paul also tells the Corinthians to forbid speaking in tongues.
Paul's last line here is about how everything must be done. In what manner?
